intro: Clarity turns recorded interviews into accurate transcripts linked to the sound, and helps you correct and organise them. It also keeps your photos, films and documents, and makes all of these into albums, e-books and documents to share with family and others – all on your own computer.

stages.title: Albums and books
stages.says: Gather interviews, photos and documents for an audience, and make them into web pages, e-books and books.

cards.title: How Clarity fits together
cards.body:
Clarity has three layers. Each builds on the one before.

1. **The Library** – everything you keep: interviews, photos, films, sound clips and documents, arranged in folders. A **series** is a folder for interviews that belong together – with one person, or on one subject.
2. **Albums** – a chosen, ordered selection from the Library for a particular audience, such as the family. Nothing is moved or copied: the same photo can be in several albums.
3. **Making the album** – turning an album into something to give people: a web page, an e-book, or a book to read in a browser. The album itself doesn't change.

A single interview can also go out on its own: as a Word or PDF document (**Save as**), or to the interviewee to check (**Send for checking…**).

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in · Where its words may go, and who may see it

cards.title: How an album decides what goes in
cards.body:
**An album only points to things.** Nothing moves in the Library. Taking something out of an album leaves it in the Library.

**Three things decide whether something can go in:**

1. **Its status.** Interviews must be **Final** (and approved by the interviewee). Photos and other things need only be **Checked**.
2. **Who may see it:** the family, particular people, an archive, the public – or **Not to be shown**. Set it on a folder and everything inside takes it; a 🔑 marks something with its own setting, ⛔ means Not to be shown.
3. **Who the album is for:** chosen when you make the album (**For**).

**The album's status** is in the badge beside its title: **✓ Ready to make**, or **⚠ Not ready** with how many things are still to do. Click it to see the list.

**Two ways round the rules, for one album only:**
- **Leave out of this album** – it stays listed with the album, under *Left out of this album*, but isn't in it. **Put it in** brings it back.
- **Clear for this album only…** – it goes in although it isn't ready, with a note of who agreed.

**Not to be shown always wins,** unless you clear it for that album.

**Related:** Why isn't my album ready? · Where its words may go, and who may see it

cards.title: Where its words may go, and who may see it
cards.body:
Clarity has two separate settings. They answer different questions.

**Where its words may go** – which *services* may receive an interview's words. Shown beside the title, e.g. **🔒 Stays on this computer**.
- *Stays on this computer:* no AI, and copies go by hand or USB stick only.
- *AgentAUS:* AgentAUS's AI may be used; it keeps the data in Australia.
- *Any cloud service:* overseas AI services may be used. Only for interviews that aren't sensitive.

Click the badge to change it. A series sets it for all its interviews.

**Who may see it** – which *people* something may go to in albums and copies: the family, particular people, an archive, the public, or **Not to be shown**. Its **⋯** › **🔑 Who may see it…**.

**In short:** the first is about computers and services, the second about people.

**Related:** Say who may see something · How Clarity fits together

cards.title: Practise on the sample interview

show.text: Click **⚙ Settings**, at the bottom of the tools on the right.
Click **Sample interview**. The made-up interview opens, with its recording.

cards.body:
**Why:** a safe place to learn: nothing you do to the sample interview matters, so you can try everything before working on a real one.

1. Click **⚙ Settings** at the bottom of the tools on the right.
2. At the top of Settings, click **Sample interview**.
3. The made-up interview opens. Click **▶ Play** and follow the words as they're spoken.

**What it is:** a made-up interview with its recording. Nothing you do to it matters, so it's the place to try things out.

**Next:** Play the recording and follow the text · Fix a word that's wrong all through

cards.title: Find your way around the window

show.text: **📚 Library** – everything you keep. Press it again to go back to your transcript.
**＋ Add** – bring work in: recordings to transcribe, a transcript someone sent you, dictation.
**? Help** – this help. F1 opens it too.
The player: **▶ Play**, back and forward 5 seconds, the speed, and **Follow**.
**Options** holds Pause while typing, Name every paragraph and Spellcheck.
The tools, in the order you'll usually need them: Transcribe, Tidy, Find, Notes, Summarise, Save as – and Settings at the bottom. Each has a **?** for its help.
**↶ Undo** and **↷ Redo**. Ctrl+Z undoes almost anything.

cards.body:
- **📚 Library** (top left) – everything you keep. Press it again to go back to your transcript.
- **＋ Add ▾** – bring work in: recordings to transcribe, a transcript someone sent you, or dictation.
- **↶ Undo** and **↷ Redo** (top right) – Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y do the same.
- **The player** – ▶ Play, −5s / +5s, the speed, and **Follow**. **Options ▾** at its right end holds *Pause while typing*, *Name every paragraph* and *Spellcheck*.
- **Messages** appear under the player, one at a time. If there are more, a link such as *+1 more message* shows the rest.
- **The tools down the right**, in the order you'll usually need them: Transcribe · Tidy · Find · Notes · Summarise · Save as · and Settings at the bottom. Hover over one to see its name.
- **Out of the way for now:** **›** in a panel's title bar (or in Help's) folds it to a narrow strip at the side, with its name showing. Click the strip to have it back just as it was; **✕** closes it. **‹ hide** does the same for the Library list.
- **⋯** beside an item in the Library or an album, or beside words you've selected, shows what you can do with it. Right-clicking does the same (on a Mac: Control-click, or click with two fingers).

**Related:** Practise on the sample interview · How Clarity fits together

cards.title: Report a problem

show.text: Click **⚙ Settings**.
Open **Problem reports**.
Click **Make a problem report…**.
Type a sentence or two about what happened, then **Update the report with this**.
Read the report – nothing private is in it.
Then **Send to Ian**, or **Save to a file** and email it.

cards.body:
**Why:** if something goes wrong, the report tells Ian what Clarity was doing and on what kind of computer, so it can be put right – without anything private in it.

1. Click **⚙ Settings** › **Problem reports** › **Make a problem report…** (or **Report this problem** on a transcription that failed).
2. Type a sentence or two about what happened, then **Update the report with this**.
3. Read the report. Then **Send to Ian**, or **Save to a file** and email it.

**What's in it:** this computer and what Clarity was doing. No transcripts, recordings, notes or lists; file and folder names are hidden.

**Include what I looked for in ? Help** (ticked) adds the searches that found nothing and your *Did this help?* answers – they help improve the help.

cards.title: Transcribe a recording

show.text: Click **＋ Add** at the top.
Click **Recordings to transcribe…**
Click **Choose recordings…** and pick a recording. Then press **Next**.
Choose how many people are talking – **Two – an interview** for most.
Leave **Standard** unless the recording is hard to hear.
Click **Start transcribing**. That's it – you can keep working meanwhile.

cards.body:
**Why:** to turn a recorded interview into text you can read, search, correct and share – with every sentence linked to the moment it was said.

1. Click **＋ Add ▾** at the top, then **Recordings to transcribe…**. (Or drag the recording onto Clarity's window.)
2. Click **Choose recordings…** and pick the recording.
3. Under **Number of speakers**, choose *Two – an interview* (or as many as are talking).
4. Leave **Quality of transcription** on *Standard – faster* unless the recording is hard to hear.
5. Click **Start transcribing**.

**How long:** roughly as long as the recording on a typical Windows laptop, and faster on a powerful PC. A recent Mac (M1 or later) is much faster: about ten minutes per hour of interview. You can keep working meanwhile.

**When it's done:** the transcript appears in the Library marked *New – please check*.

**The first time:** Clarity asks before downloading what it needs. Allow time for the download.

**Several recordings?** Hold Ctrl while choosing. They're done one after another with the same settings.

**Related:** Play the recording and follow the text · Speakers: name them and fix who's speaking

cards.title: Open a transcript someone sent you

show.text: Click **＋ Add**.
Click **A transcript someone sent you…**, then choose the file you downloaded.

cards.body:
**Why:** to carry on working on a transcript someone else made in Clarity or DocAnalyser, or to bring in a whole library they've handed over.

1. If it came by email or Google Drive, **download it first** and save it.
2. Click **＋ Add ▾** at the top, then **A transcript someone sent you…**, and choose the file.
3. If you already have it, choose **Replace mine** (a backup is kept) or **Keep both**.

**Other ways:** drag the file onto Clarity's window, or double-click it.

**Works for:** a .clarity or .docanalyser file (one transcript), or a .clarity-library file (a whole library).

**Related:** Save as Word or PDF · How Clarity fits together

cards.title: Dictate instead of typing

show.text: Click **＋ Add**.
Click **Dictate…**.
Click to start, and speak. Say *new paragraph* to start one. Click again to finish.

cards.body:
**Why:** to compose by voice – notes, a passage for an album, a summary – where speaking is quicker or easier than typing.

1. Click **＋ Add ▾** at the top, then **Dictate…**.
2. Click **● Start dictating** and speak. Punctuation comes by itself; say *new paragraph* to start one.
3. Pause and carry on as you need. Click **■ Finish** to make a new transcript in the Library.

**Check the microphone first:** ⚙ Settings › Microphone.

**Related:** Transcribe a recording

cards.title: Get a recording from a phone
cards.body:
**Why:** most interviews are now recorded on a phone. The recording has to reach the computer before Clarity can transcribe it – and for a private interview, by a route that doesn't leave copies on someone else's servers.

1. Record with the phone's own recorder (iPhone: Voice Memos; Android: Recorder).
2. Send it to the computer – whichever suits:
   - **Android:** Quick Share to the PC (it arrives in Downloads), or a cable (choose *File transfer* on the phone).
   - **iPhone:** LocalSend, free from localsend.org, on the phone and the PC, over your own Wi-Fi.
   - **Any phone:** WhatsApp a message to yourself, as a *Document*, then save it on the computer.
3. Drag the recording onto Clarity's window, or **＋ Add ▾** › **Recordings to transcribe…**.

**Private interviews:** WhatsApp, email and cloud drives keep a copy on their servers. Delete the recording from the phone and Downloads once it's in Clarity, and turn off the phone's cloud backup of recordings.

**For a good recording:** phone flat on the table between the speakers, Do Not Disturb on.

**Related:** Transcribe a recording

cards.title: Play the recording and follow the text

show.text: Click **▶ Play**. The sentence being spoken is highlighted.
Keep **Follow** ticked so the text keeps up with the recording.
**Options** holds *Pause while typing* – the recording waits while you type. Click it to see.
Leave this ticked. Press **Next**.
When a word is wrong, click on it and type. It's saved by itself.

cards.body:
**Why:** transcription is never perfect. Listening while you read is how you catch the words it got wrong – and the link between text and sound means you can always go back and hear exactly what was said.

1. Click **▶ Play** (or press Ctrl+Space). The sentence being spoken is highlighted.
2. Keep **Follow** ticked so the text keeps up with the recording.
3. When a word is wrong, click on it and type the correction. It's saved by itself.
4. Missed something? Press Ctrl+Shift+Space to hear the last few seconds again.

**Pause while typing** (under **Options ▾**) pauses the recording while you type, then goes back 2 seconds and carries on.

**Handy:**
- **Hear a paragraph:** click its time on the left, such as [04:22].
- **Play from a sentence:** hold Alt and click the sentence.
- **Slower or faster:** the speed box, from 0.75× to 1.5×.

**Good to know:** a plain click in the text never starts the recording; it just puts the cursor there. Next time you open the transcript, Clarity offers to carry on where you stopped.

**Related:** Fix a word that's wrong all through · Speakers: name them and fix who's speaking

cards.title: Fix a word that's wrong all through

show.text: Click **Find** (the magnifying glass).
Type the wrong word – or select it in the transcript and drag it in. Every place is listed below.
Under **Replace…**, type the right word.
Look down the places. Untick any to leave alone.
Click **Change ticked**. One Ctrl+Z undoes them all.

cards.body:
**Why:** transcription often gets the same word wrong all the way through – a name, a place, a local word. Fixing it once, everywhere, saves finding each one by hand.

1. Select the wrong word in the transcript, click the **⋯** that appears beside it (or right-click it) and choose **Replace…**. **Find** opens with the word filled in.
2. Type the right word in **Replace with**.
3. Look down the list of places. Untick any to leave alone.
4. Click **Change ticked**.

**Changed your mind?** Ctrl+Z. One undo reverses them all.

**Fix it in future transcripts too:** use **Also save to** before changing, so later transcripts are checked for it.

**A name spelt several different ways?** See *Fix a name spelt several ways*.

**Related:** Fix a name spelt several ways

cards.title: Fix a name spelt several ways

show.text: Click **Find** (the magnifying glass).
Leave this box **empty**, so the whole transcript is checked.
Open **Misspellings**.
Click **Scan for names spelt several ways**.
Click the right spelling of a name. Its other spellings are listed, ticked. *Read each place* and untick any that are really right.
Click **Change ticked**. Then do the next name.

cards.body:
**Why:** transcription often spells one name several ways in a single interview. Getting names right matters most of all – to the family, to an archive, and for anyone searching later.

1. Open **Find** (the magnifying glass on the right), open **Misspellings**, and leave the box empty.
2. Click **Scan for names spelt several ways**.
3. Click the right spelling, then review the places it found.
4. **Read each place before changing it.** Untick any that are really right, then change the rest.

**Sometimes the odd spelling is the point.** In "they got my name wrong, called me Pettigrove", the wrong name is being quoted. Leave it unticked.

**Fix speakers before tidying the paragraphs:** tidying joins paragraphs by the same speaker, so a wrong speaker gets merged in.

**Related:** Make a name list so names come out right · Fix a word that's wrong all through

cards.title: Make a name list so names come out right

show.text: Click **Find** (the magnifying glass).
Click **📋 Name lists…**.
Click **New name list**.
Give the list a name – e.g. *Solomon Islands*.
Type or paste the names, one per line.
**Or** describe the subject here – e.g. *villages in the south of France* – then use **Copy the request** (for an AI chat you already use) or **Build this list for me**.
Click **Save list**. To use it, tick it under Lists – or, before transcribing, in **Transcribe** › **Tick a name list…**

cards.body:
**Why:** transcription often mishears names – "Kutamundra" for Cootamundra – and spells one name several ways. A **name list** gives it the right spellings for a subject, so more come out right first time and the rest are easy to find.

1. Open **Find** on the right › **📋 Name lists…**, and click **New name list**.
2. Give it a **List name**, and type or paste the names, one per line.
3. Or describe the **Subject** (e.g. "villages in the south of France") and let AI find the names:
   - **Copy the request** – paste it into an AI chat you already use, then paste its answer back into the names box. Nothing goes online from Clarity.
   - **Build this list for me** – Clarity asks an AI service itself (needs cloud services and a key in ⚙ Settings). Only the subject is sent.
4. Look the names over (AI gets spellings wrong too), then **Save list**.

**Best used before transcribing:** in **Transcribe**, click **Tick a name list…** (just above **More choices**) and tick the list. The first 40 or so names go to the transcription engine as hints, so more come out right first time.

**Any time afterwards:** in Find › Misspellings, tick the lists that fit and press **Check against the ticked lists**.

**Tip:** split a big subject into smaller lists, so you can tick just the ones that fit each interview.

**Related:** Fix a name spelt several ways · Transcribe a recording

cards.title: Speakers: name them and fix who's speaking

show.text: Click a coloured name label at the start of a paragraph.
To rename a speaker everywhere (*A* to *Peg*), type the new name in the **Rename … everywhere** box and press Enter.
Or give this paragraph a different speaker: choose one above, or type a name here and press Enter.

cards.body:
**Why:** a transcript is only clear if each person's words are under their own name. Clarity guesses who is speaking; it's often right, but not always.

1. Click the coloured name label at the start of a paragraph. After transcribing, speakers are labelled *A*, *B*, *C*… – *A* is whoever talks most.
2. Choose the right speaker. Or type a name in the **New speaker…** box and press Enter.
3. **To rename a speaker everywhere** (e.g. *A* to *Peg*): click a name label and type the new name under **Rename … everywhere to:**, then press Enter.

**Several paragraphs at once:** click in the first, Shift+click in the last, then right-click (on a Mac, Control-click) and choose the speaker.

**Quicker:** Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+9 sets the speaker; Ctrl+0 clears it.

**Related:** Play the recording and follow the text

cards.title: Leave a passage out of an interview

show.text: Select the sentences to leave out, then click the **⋯** that appears beside them (or right-click them).
Click **✂ Cut this sentence** (or **Cut these … sentences**, or **Cut this paragraph**) **from the interview**.
The passage is marked as cut – in the words and the sound. **▶ Hear across the cut** lets you check how it sounds. **Put back** restores it.

cards.body:
**Why:** interviewees sometimes say things that shouldn't go further – a private matter, something about someone else, a passage they ask to have removed. Cutting it leaves it out of the words and the sound in everything you hand on, while the full recording stays with you.

1. Select the sentences to leave out – only those sentences, unless you mean the whole paragraph.
2. Click the **⋯** beside them (or right-click) and choose **✂ Cut this sentence from the interview** (or **Cut these … sentences**, for several).
3. Click **▶ Hear across the cut** to check how it sounds without them.

**In albums and copies:** the passage is left out of the words *and* the sound, and *[edited 0:11]* marks the place. Nothing is deleted: **Put back** restores it.

**Read on past the cut.** The next line may answer what you've taken out. Cut or reword that too.

**Related:** Play the recording and follow the text

cards.title: Tidy up: ums, repeats, paragraphs and punctuation

show.text: Click **Tidy**.
Click **Check transcript**.
Look down the suggestions. The surer ones start ticked; untick any you don't want.
Click **Apply ticked**. One Ctrl+Z undoes the lot.

cards.body:
**Why:** raw transcripts are full of ums, repeated words and fragments. Tidying makes the text easier to read, while you decide what stays.

1. Click **Tidy** on the right (or press Ctrl+Shift+T).
2. Click **Check transcript**. Clarity lists suggested clean-ups across the whole transcript: joining pieces into paragraphs, splitting long ones, capitals and punctuation, repeated words and fillers, and gaps in the speech worth listening to.
3. Look down the list. The surer suggestions start ticked, matters of taste unticked. Tick or untick as you like.
4. Click **Apply ticked**.

**Nothing changes until you apply,** and one Ctrl+Z undoes the lot.

**Need a word-for-word (verbatim) transcript?** Leave the ums and repeats unticked.

**Fix speakers first:** joining paragraphs puts together those by the same speaker, so a wrong speaker gets merged in.

**Related:** Speakers: name them and fix who's speaking · Play the recording and follow the text

cards.title: Add a note to myself

show.text: Select some words, then click the **⋯** that appears beside them (or right-click).
Click **Add a note…**, type the note, and you're done. A ✎ marks the line.

cards.body:
**Why:** to leave yourself a reminder at the exact place in the transcript – a name to check, a question to ask the interviewee – without changing the words.

1. Select some words (or put the cursor on a word).
2. Click the **⋯** beside them (or right-click) › **Add a note…**, or press Ctrl+Alt+M.
3. Type the note, such as "check this name" or "ask about this".

A **✎** beside the line marks each note. Click it to read, edit, resolve or delete it. **Notes** on the right lists them all.

**Notes stay with their words** as you edit, and are left out of copies unless you choose to include them.

**Related:** Play the recording and follow the text

cards.title: Put interviews in folders or a series

show.text: Click **＋ Folder**, and type its name.
Drag things onto the folder – or click their **⋯** › **Move to…**.
To make the folder a series, click its **⋯** (or right-click it).
Click **Make it a series**.

cards.body:
**Why:** folders keep interviews and their photos together and easy to find. A series also lets Clarity work across all of one person's interviews at once – an index, summaries, themes – and an album can start from it and keep up with it.

1. Open **📚 Library** and click **＋ Folder**. Type its name.
2. To move things in, drag them onto the folder, or click their **⋯** › **Move to…**.
3. **To make it a series** (interviews that belong together – with one person, or on one subject): click the folder's **⋯** › **Make it a series**. A series also keeps the interviewee, interviewer, project and where their words may go.

**Several at once:** Ctrl+click or Shift+click to pick them.

**Related:** Mark an interview as checked or final · How Clarity fits together

cards.title: Mark an interview as checked or final

show.text: Click the status beside the title.
Choose **Checked**, **Being reviewed** or **Final**.

cards.body:
**Why:** the status says how far each interview has got, so you can see at a glance what still needs work – and albums use it: interviews go in only once they're Final, photos and other things once they're Checked.

1. Click the status label beside the interview's title (for example *New – please check*).
2. Choose **Checked**, **Being reviewed** or **Final**.

**What they mean:** *Checked* – corrected against the recording; *Being reviewed* – a copy is with the interviewee; *Final* – their changes are made.

**Why it matters:** interviews go into albums once they're **Final**; photos and other things once they're **Checked**.

**Other ways:** its **⋯** in the Library, or use its details on the right.

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in

cards.title: Say who may see something

show.text: Click **⋯** beside a folder, a series, or one thing (or right-click it).
Click **🔑 Who may see…** (for a folder: everything in it).
Say whether permission was given, choose who may see it, then **Save**.

cards.body:
**Why:** Clarity asks this so nothing goes to the wrong people: an album only includes what's cleared for its audience. A permission given for a whole family folder saves setting it item by item.

**Whether you have permission – the top of the same box:**
- **Not yet recorded** – nobody has said either way.
- **Given** – who gave it, when, and how: a signed form, an email or letter, or spoken on the recording. **Attach the form, email or letter…** keeps a copy with it; **Attach another…** adds more.
- **Not needed** – with the reason: it's your own, it's out of copyright, it's already published.
- **Refused**, or **Given, then withdrawn** – it stays in the Library and is left out of every album and copy.

A permission with an end date holds the thing back from albums once that date has passed.

**What still needs it:** in the Library, **🔑 Permission not recorded** (under **Everything**) lists every interview, photo and other item nobody has said either way about. Recording it once on a folder covers everything in the folder.

**For everything in a folder at once:**
1. Click the folder's (or series') **⋯** and choose **🔑 Who may see everything in it…**.
2. Choose **The family**, and tick an archive or the public too if that's agreed. Save.

**For one thing that's different:**
1. Click its **⋯** and choose **🔑 Who may see it…**.
2. Choose, for example, **Not to be shown**, or particular people. Save. It shows 🔑, or ⛔ for Not to be shown.
3. **As its folder says** removes the exception.

**Not the same as where its words may go** (the badge beside a transcript's title), which is about AI and other services.

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in · Where its words may go, and who may see it

cards.title: Find an interview, or a word across all of them

show.text: Type a name, a place or a word. The list narrows to the interviews that have it.

cards.body:
**Why:** to find which interview mentions a person, place or event, without opening each one.

1. Click **📚 Library**.
2. Type in the search box above the list (*Search titles and words…*).
3. The list narrows to the interviews whose title or words match. Double-click one to open it.

**Within one transcript:** open **Find** on the right (Ctrl+F).

**Related:** Fix a word that's wrong all through

cards.title: Get back something I deleted

show.text: Click **🗑 Recycle Bin**, at the foot of the Library list.
Click **⋯** beside what you want back, in the list on the right (or right-click it).
Click **Restore**.

cards.body:
**Why:** deleting only moves things to the Recycle Bin, so a mistake can be undone.

1. Click **📚 Library**. At the foot of the list is **🗑 Recycle Bin**.
2. Click **⋯** beside what you want back (or right-click it) and choose **Restore**. It goes back where it was.

**A change inside a transcript?** Ctrl+Z (Undo) goes back step by step.

**Empty the Bin…** and **Delete for good…** can't be undone.

cards.title: Back up or move my work

show.text: Click **⚙ Settings**.
Open **Where your work is kept**.
**Show it in its folder** – then copy that folder to a USB stick or backup drive.
Or **Move my work to another folder…** to keep it on another drive.

cards.body:
**Why:** a computer can fail, be lost or be stolen; a copy somewhere else means years of interviews aren't lost with it.

Clarity keeps everything – transcripts, recordings, lists, libraries – in one folder. That's the folder to back up.

1. Click **⚙ Settings** › **Where your work is kept**. It shows the folder.
2. **Show it in its folder** opens it, to copy to a USB stick or backup drive.
3. To move it (to another drive, say): **Move my work to another folder…**. Clarity copies it, checks it all arrived, and carries on from there.

**Clarity's own backups:** one each time it opens, in *data\backups*; the last ten are kept.

**Private interviews:** avoid a synced OneDrive folder – anything in it is copied to Microsoft's cloud.

**Related:** Pass a whole library to someone

cards.title: Add photos, films, sounds or documents

show.text: In the Library list, click the folder or series they belong with.
Click **＋ Media** and choose them – or drag them onto the window.

cards.body:
**Why:** photos, films, letters and documents sit with the interviews they belong to, so you can place them beside the words and put them into albums for the family.

1. In **📚 Library**, choose the folder or series they belong with.
2. Click **＋ Media** above the list and choose them – or drag them from your computer onto the window.

A whole folder of photos, or a zip file of them (as sent by email or downloaded), can be dragged on just the same: Clarity takes out the photos and PDF documents inside, and tells you about anything it left.

Your originals are copied in, untouched. A film or sound file: Clarity asks whether it's a clip to keep or an interview to transcribe. A Word file: whether it's a typed transcript or a document to keep (kept as a PDF copy).

**Name and caption them** next – see *Name and caption photos, one after another*.

**Related:** Name and caption photos, one after another · Make an album for the family

cards.title: Tidy photos of paintings

show.text: Click **⋯** beside a photo or a folder (or right-click several chosen).
Click **✨ Tidy…** (or **Tidy it again…**). Then look at the flagged ones first: **Fix the edges…**, **Adjust…**.

cards.body:
**Why:** photos of paintings are often taken at an angle, with the frame or wall around them, or in poor light. Tidying straightens and trims them and evens the colour, so the painting itself is what you see.

1. Click **⋯** beside a photo or a folder, or right-click several chosen › **✨ Tidy…**.
2. In the review, look at the flagged ones first.
3. **Fix the edges…** to drag the corners; **Adjust…** for brightness, warmth and lighting.

**Changed your mind?** Its **⋯** › **Undo the tidying**, at any time. The original is kept.

**Related:** Rescue small, grainy or old photos

cards.title: Rescue small, grainy or old photos

show.text: Click **⋯** beside a photo (or right-click it).
Click **✨ Enhance…** (or **Enhance again…**), say what kind of picture it is, then **Try it**.

cards.body:
**Why:** old snapshots and newspaper pictures are often small or grainy; enhancing makes them clearer in an album or e-book, especially on a large screen.

1. Click **⋯** beside a photo (or right-click it) › **✨ Enhance…**.
2. Say whether it's a photo or a printed (newspaper) picture, and how grainy it is.
3. Click **Try it** and compare. Set the **Strength**.
4. **Keep it**, or **Leave it**.

**Related:** Tidy photos of paintings

cards.title: Save as Word or PDF

show.text: Click **Save as** on the right.
Choose **Word (.docx)** – or PDF.
The preview shows how it will look. Tick what to include above it.
Click to save it. It opens when it's ready.

cards.body:
**Why:** a Word or PDF copy is easy to share, print or keep, by anyone, without Clarity.

1. Click **Save as** on the right (or press Ctrl+Shift+E).
2. Under **Format**, choose *Word (.docx)* or *PDF (.pdf)*.
3. Choose what to include, such as names, timestamps and notes. The preview shows how it will look.
4. Click **Save as Word** (or **Save as PDF**).

**Where it goes:** it opens when saved. Nothing is ever overwritten.

**For someone to carry on editing in Clarity:** choose the format *Clarity file* instead.

**Related:** Send a transcript to the interviewee to check

cards.title: Send a transcript to the interviewee to check

show.text: Click **⋯** beside the transcript in the Library list (or right-click it).
Click **✉ Send for checking…**.
Choose a page to open in a web browser (they hear the recording), or a Word document.

show.target: text=What they send comes back to
show.text: Fill in your email (or WhatsApp) and your name, then **Make it**.

cards.body:
**Why:** the interviewee is the best judge of whether a transcript says what they meant – names, places, a misheard phrase. Their corrections and their approval are what make a transcript Final.

1. Click **⋯** beside the transcript in the Library (or right-click it) and choose **✉ Send for checking…**.
2. Under **Send it as**, choose *A page to open in a web browser* (they hear the recording as they read – best for most people) or *A Word document* (words only).
3. Under **What they send comes back to**, fill in your email (or WhatsApp) and **Your name**. Clarity remembers these.
4. Click **Make it**, then send the file however suits: email, USB stick or a shared folder.

**While it's out:** the transcript shows *Out for correcting*. Leave those paragraphs alone until it comes back, so their corrections still fit.

**Related:** Bring in the corrections they sent back

cards.title: Bring in the corrections they sent back

show.text: Save the attachment first. Then click **⋯** beside the transcript in the Library list (or right-click it).
Click **Bring in corrections…** and choose the saved file. Untick any changes you don't want.

cards.body:
**Why:** the interviewee's corrections come back in one small file; bringing them in puts them straight into the transcript, beside yours, so nothing is retyped and you choose what to accept.

1. **Save the attachment first.** Download the file from the email; it can't be dragged straight out of Gmail.
2. Click **⋯** beside the transcript in the Library (or right-click it) and choose **Bring in corrections…**, then pick the file. (Or drag the saved file onto Clarity.)
3. Each changed paragraph is shown beside yours. Untick any you don't want, then take the rest.

**Their comments** come in as notes, marked with their name.

**Afterwards:** mark the transcript **Final**.

**Related:** Send a transcript to the interviewee to check · Mark an interview as checked or final

cards.title: Turn on summaries and other AI features

show.text: Click **⚙ Settings**.
Open **Privacy and cloud services**.
Allow cloud services when you choose, pick a service and enter its key. **AgentAUS** keeps interviews in Australia.
Click **Test the chosen service**.

cards.body:
**Why:** summaries, themes and key points are made by an AI service online. They're off until you choose one, so nothing leaves your computer unless you decide it should.

1. Click **⚙ Settings** › **Privacy and cloud services**.
2. Choose to allow cloud services only when you choose.
3. Under **AI services**, choose a service and enter its key. **AgentAUS** keeps your interviews in Australia.
4. Click **Test the chosen service**.

**Why they're off at first:** AI features send text to an online service. Transcribing, editing and the index of names and places work without them.

**Each interview decides too:** the badge beside its title (e.g. *Words may go to AgentAUS*) says which services may see it.

**Related:** Make a summary, themes or an index · Where its words may go, and who may see it

cards.title: Make a summary, themes or an index

show.text: Click **Summarise**.
Check what you're working on – this interview, or its series.
Choose what to make: a summary, themes, key points, a topic, or the index. Each result is kept in the Library under the interview.

cards.body:
**Why:** once a transcript is finished, a summary, the themes with their times, or an index of names and places helps others find their way into a long interview – for an archive's catalogue, or a family's quick look.

1. Open the finished transcript and click **Summarise** on the right.
2. Under **Working on**, choose this interview, or a folder or series it's in.
3. Choose what to make and click its button: **Make the summary**, **Find the themes**, **List the key points**, **Find it** (a topic you type), or **Make the index** (names and places).
4. The result is kept in the Library, under its interview. The transcript itself isn't changed.

**The index is made on this computer;** nothing is sent anywhere. The others use an AI service, and only one that the interview's words may go to (see the badge beside its title).

**Buttons greyed out?** No AI service is set up yet, or the interview's words stay on this computer. See **Settings** › Privacy and cloud services.

**Related:** Where its words may go, and who may see it

cards.title: Pass a transcript to someone to keep editing

show.text: Click **Save as**.
Choose **Clarity file**.
Click to save the file, then send it – by a Drive link if it's big.

cards.body:
**Why:** for someone else to carry on correcting or using a transcript in their own Clarity (or DocAnalyser), with its recording and everything you've done to it.

1. Open it, then **Save as** on the right.
2. Under **Format**, choose *Clarity file*, then **Save the file to pass on**.
3. Send them the file. With the recording it's usually too big to email: share it by a OneDrive or Google Drive link.

**At their end:** **＋ Add ▾** › **A transcript someone sent you…**.

**Related:** Open a transcript someone sent you · Pass a whole library to someone

cards.title: Pass a whole library to someone

show.text: Click the library's name (at the top of the window, or of the list).
Click **Export this library…** and save the file. Give it to them on a USB stick or by a Drive link.

cards.body:
**Why:** to hand the whole collection to someone else – an archive, a family member, whoever carries on the work – or to move it to another computer, with everything in it.

1. Click the library's name at the top of the list (**📚 My library ▾**).
2. Choose **Export this library…** and save the file.
3. Give them the file (USB stick, or a Google Drive link).

**At their end:** **＋ Add ▾** › **A transcript someone sent you…** and choose the .clarity-library file – or **Import a library…** from the same library menu.

**Just one folder or series?** Its **⋯** › **Export as a library…**.

**Related:** Back up or move my work · Pass a transcript to someone to keep editing

cards.title: Make a family album in three steps

show.text: Click **＋ Add**.
Click **A family album…**.
**Whose story?** Choose the person's series or folder.
The album's name is filled in – change it if you like.
Click **Next**. Clarity gathers everything, then asks a plain question about anything that isn't ready yet; then you choose a web page, an e-book or a book to read in a browser.

cards.body:
**Why:** the quickest way to give a family one person's story – their interviews, photos and documents – without learning how albums work first.

1. Click **＋ Add** › **A family album…** – or click **⋯** beside the person's series or folder › **Make a family album from this…**.
2. **Whose story?** Choose the series or folder, and click **Next**. If it has folders inside it, **Arrange it** lets you choose a section for each folder instead of one for each kind of thing.
3. **What goes in:** everything in it goes in, in sections. For anything not ready yet, Clarity asks one question for the whole group – *Is it finished?*, *Has he read and approved them?*, *Have you looked at them?*, *May the family see these?* – and you answer **Yes** or **Leave them out for now**. Anything marked not to be shown is left out.
4. **How to give it:** a **web page**, an **e-book** or a **book to read in a browser**, then **Next – make it**.

What you get is an ordinary album, kept up to date with the series: anything left out is listed at its foot, to put in later, and you can add captions, your own words or change the order with the album tools.

**Related:** Make an album for the family · Why isn't my album ready?

cards.title: Make an album for the family

show.text: Click **＋ Album**.
Give the album a name.
Choose who it's for – *The interviewee and family*, say.
Choose the interviewee's series here. *Keep up with it* then appears just below – leave it ticked, so things added to the series later join the album.
Click **Make it**. Then look at the badge beside the album's title: ✓ Ready to make, or what's still to do.

cards.body:
**Why:** an album gathers interviews, photos and documents for one audience – the family, an archive, the public – in the order they'll read them. Everything you make to give people (a web page, an e-book, a book to read in a browser) is made from an album.

1. Open **📚 Library**, then click **＋ Album**.
2. Give it a **Name**, choose **For** *The interviewee and family*, and **Start from** the interviewee's series.
3. **Keep up with it** appears once a series is chosen: leave it ticked, so things added to the series later join the album. If the series has folders inside it, **Arrange it** appears too: choose *As its folders* to start the album with a section for each folder, rather than one for each kind of thing.
4. Check the badge beside the album's title. If it says **⚠ Not ready**, see *Why isn't my album ready?*
5. Arrange it: **＋ Sections…** for headings, and **✎ Name and caption photos…** for the photos.
6. Click **Make ▾** › **Make an album to look through in a browser…** (search it, click a sentence to hear it, and – if you allow – add to it), or **Make an e-book…**, or **Make a book to read in a browser…**.

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in · Why isn't my album ready?

cards.title: Why isn't my album ready?

show.text: Click the badge beside the album's title – **⚠ Not ready** (or ✓ Ready to make, when nothing's left). It takes you to the list of what's still to do.

Each item in the list says why it's held back, with the link that fixes it – **Mark it Checked**, **Record the interviewee's approval (today)**, **Who may see it…**, **Leave out of this album**, **Clear for this album only…**.

cards.title: Put an album into sections, in order

show.text: Click **＋ Sections…** and type the headings, one per line.
Then drag things onto the headings, and drag to change the order. The order here is the order in everything you make.

cards.body:
**Why:** the album's order is the order people meet things in whatever you make from it – the web page, the e-book, the book to read in a browser. Its sections become the chapters, and the e-book's and book's contents page.

1. In the album, click **＋ Sections…** and type the headings, such as *The bakery*, *The flood*.
2. Put things under them: drag each onto a heading. To move several at once, hold Ctrl and click each one (or hold Shift and click the last of a run), then drag any one of them – or right-click it › **Move to…**.
3. Drag to change the order. A heading's **⋯** has **Rename…**, **↑ Move up**, **↓ Move down**, **Move to…** (with everything in it), **＋ Section inside…** and **Remove the section**.

**Already arranged in folders?** Click **⋯** beside the album › **Start my sections from the folders in** … to get a section for each folder inside the one the album started from, with each thing under its folder's heading. Sections go two levels deep, so a folder deeper than that has its own section at the second level. It's a copy to start from: change it as you like, and nothing changes in your folders.

**Related:** Make an album for the family · Name and caption photos, one after another

cards.title: Name and caption photos, one after another

show.text: Click **✎ Name and caption photos…**.
Type the name, press Enter, type the caption, then Ctrl+Enter for the next one. Esc to stop.

cards.body:
**Why:** names and captions say who and what is in each picture. They go with the photo into albums, e-books and exports, and are often the only record of who's who once the people who knew have gone.

1. Click **⋯** beside a photo, or right-click several chosen › **Name and caption them, one by one…** – or in an album, **✎ Name and caption photos…**.
2. Type the name, press Enter, type the caption.
3. Press Ctrl+Enter to save and go on to the next. Esc to stop.

**See more of the picture:** drag the bar under it down. Name and Caption always stay in view.

**A different caption in one album only:** click **⋯** on the photo in that album.

**Related:** Put an album into sections, in order · Add photos, films, sounds or documents

cards.title: Add your own words to an album

show.text: Click **＋ Add ▾**.

show.target: text=Write a passage to add to the album…
show.text: Click **Write a passage to add to the album…**, give it a title and type the words.

cards.body:
**Why:** an introduction, a note between sections or a few words of explanation help readers understand what they're looking at and why it matters.

1. In the album, click **＋ Add ▾** › **Write a passage to add to the album…**.
2. Give it a title and type or paste the words.
3. Move it into place like anything else. A passage in no section comes first.

**Related:** Put an album into sections, in order

cards.title: Keep something with an album but leave it out

show.text: Click **Leave out of this album** beside the item (or its **⋯**). **Put it in** at the foot brings it back.

cards.body:
**Why:** to keep something on an album's list without putting it in this time – a photo still waiting for permission, say – so it's easy to put in later and nothing is forgotten.

1. Click **⋯** on it in the album (or right-click it) › **Leave out of this album**.
2. It moves to *Left out of this album*, at the foot of the album, with any reason it wasn't ready.
3. To bring it back, click **Put it in** beside it.

**✕ instead** takes it off the album's list altogether. It stays in the Library.

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in · Why isn't my album ready?

cards.title: Let one album have something that isn't ready

show.text: Click **Clear for this album only…** beside the item, and say who agreed.

cards.body:
**Why:** sometimes the people concerned agree to something going into one album – a family keepsake, say – though it isn't checked or cleared for that audience. This lets it in there without changing its status or who may see it anywhere else.

1. In the album, find it in the to-do list or on its row, and click **Clear for this album only…**.
2. Say who agreed and when, then confirm.
3. It shows *✓ this album only*.

**Nothing else changes:** its own status and who may see it stay as they were, and other albums still go by them.

**Related:** How an album decides what goes in · Say who may see something

cards.title: Let family arrange and add to an album

show.text: Click **Make ▾**.

show.target: text=Make an album to look through in a browser…
show.text: Click **Make an album to look through in a browser…**.
Choose what they can do, from *View only* to *Full editing*. When their file comes back, use **＋ Add ▾** › **What was sent back…** in the album.

cards.body:
**Why:** the family often knows best who's in a photo and what order the stories belong in. This lets them arrange, caption and add to their copy, and send their changes back for you to take or leave.

1. In the album, click **Make ▾** › **Make an album to look through in a browser…**.
2. Choose what they can do, from *View only* to *Full editing*. Make it and send it.
3. When their file comes back, open the album and click **＋ Add ▾** › **What was sent back…**. Each change is listed, ticked, for you to take or not.

**Related:** Make an album for the family

cards.title: Make an e-book

show.text: Click **Make ▾**.
Click **Make an e-book…**.
Choose the look and the cover. If the album has recordings, choose under **The voice**: *With the recordings* for tap-to-hear, or *The words only* for Kindle and Kobo.

cards.body:
**Why:** an e-book is a keepsake that opens in a reading app on a phone, tablet or e-reader, with the photos in place and – in apps that allow it – the voices: tap a sentence to hear it said.

1. In the album, click **Make ▾** › **Make an e-book…**.
2. Choose the look and the cover.
3. Under **The voice**, choose *With the recordings* for tap-a-sentence-to-hear, or *The words only* for Kindle, Kobo and Google Play Books.

**Note:** an e-book has no password; anyone it's forwarded to can read it.

**Related:** Make a book anyone can open · Make an album for the family

cards.title: Make a book anyone can open

show.text: Click **Make ▾**.

show.target: text=Make a book to read in a browser…
show.text: Click **Make a book to read in a browser…**. Keep the password, give it to them separately, and share the file by a Google Drive link.

cards.body:
**Why:** for people who'd struggle with an e-book reader: they click a link and the book opens in any web browser, on a phone or a computer, with nothing to install. The password keeps it among the people you give it to.

1. In the album, click **Make ▾** › **Make a book to read in a browser…**.
2. Leave the password ticked, and give it to them separately.
3. Put the file on Google Drive and share it as *Anyone with the link*. Clarity shows the steps and a message to copy.
4. **Make the card** prints the instructions for them.

**Related:** Make an e-book · Make an album for the family

cards.title: Make an album as a Word or PDF document

show.text: Click **Make ▾**.

show.target: text=Make a Word or PDF copy…
show.text: Click **Make a Word or PDF copy…**.

Tick **A Word document**, **A PDF** or both, then click **Make it**. The size of the pictures, what goes under them and *Draft for comment* are under **More choices** – the line beside it says what's chosen.

cards.body:
**Why:** an ordinary document is the easiest thing to pass round for comment. Everyone can open it, in Word people can add comments and suggest changes, and it prints. It holds the album's words and pictures in the album's order: the passages you wrote, the photos with their captions, the interviews' words.

1. In the album, click **Make ▾** › **Make a Word or PDF copy…**.
2. Tick **A Word document** (best for comments), **A PDF** (looks the same on every computer), or both.
3. Click **Make it**. It opens, so you can check it.
4. Send it as an email attachment, or put it in a shared folder.

To change how it's made, open **More choices** before step 3 (the line beside it says what's chosen now):
- **Pictures:** how big they are – or *Two side by side* or *Three side by side*, which sets pictures that follow one another in rows and leaves the words the full width of the page.
- **Under each picture:** its name, its caption, and *More about it* (the story behind it).
- **Mark it “Draft for comment”** (ticked to start with), and where it's saved.

**Note:** it's a copy. What people write in it doesn't come back into the album by itself; make their changes in Clarity. There are no recordings in it: a film or sound recording is shown by its picture and caption. Tick **Protect it with a password** to lock it – send the password separately. Your own note about a picture never goes in.

**Related:** Add your own words to an album · Make an e-book

cards.title: Save photos to print and frame

show.text: Click **⋯** beside a photo or a folder of photos (or right-click several chosen).
Click **🖨 Save for printing…**.
Choose how: **As they are**, **All the same size, with a white border**, or **The pictures themselves matched**. The list shows how big each one prints well.

cards.body:
**Why:** an album's web page, e-book and Word or PDF copy all use smaller copies of the pictures, which is right for reading but not for a print on the wall. This saves each photo as a file of its own, full size and top quality, for a print service (Officeworks and the like) to print at whatever size you order. It uses what you see in Clarity: the tidied or enhanced version where there is one.

1. For one photo or a few: click **⋯** beside it (or right-click several chosen) › **🖨 Save for printing…**. For a whole album: open the album › **🖨 Save its photos for printing…**.
2. Choose how: **As they are** (each at its own size and shape); **All the same size, with a white border** (choose a print size: the whole picture sits inside it with white making up the difference, so nothing is cropped and they all fit the same frame); or **The pictures themselves matched** (the same longest side, height or width, with no border).
3. Look at the list. **Prints well up to** is how big each photo can go. *Will look soft* means it's too small for the size chosen: untick it, choose a smaller size, or **✨ Enhance** it first.
4. Under **Save them in**, choose a folder, a USB stick, or **Google Drive** (shown when Google Drive for desktop is on this computer).
5. Click **Save**. The photos go in a folder of their own, and **Show them** opens it.
6. Take the folder to the print service, or upload the files on its website. With a border, order each print at the size in its file's name and ask for no cropping.

**Note:** making a small picture bigger doesn't add detail, so it prints softer than the others. Nothing in the Library is changed, and nothing already in the folder is written over. Films, sound recordings and PDF documents are left out. From an album, anything left out of it or marked *Not to be shown* stays out.

**Related:** Tidy photos of paintings · Rescue small, grainy or old photos · Make an album as a Word or PDF document
